summary: Both R2 correctness findings are verifiably closed: DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (xi) no longer references '10 questions' (R3-VERIFY-1 CLOSED) and DISPATCH-NOTE line 36 stale references §10 Q7 and §5.5 are both gone (R3-VERIFY-2 CLOSED). However, the fix-round-2 edits introduced one new MAJ-level correctness defect: the cascade-status field spec in §5.2 item (2) defines exactly two values (onboarded / blocked-on-adopter-conflict), but the operator-bump fallback path described in R-024-07 and §6 024B requires the CI script to detect a third distinct scenario — yet no DISPATCH-NOTE field value or separate field is defined for the CI script to parse. The result is an internally inconsistent CI enforcement specification: the CI script cannot distinguish an onboarded-via-Renovate slice from an onboarded-via-operator-bump slice using only the two defined cascade-status values.

findings.title: R2-NEW-MAJ-001 closure: DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (xi) stale '(10 questions)' replaced with accurate explanatory note
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md criterion (xi) now reads: '§10 captures only genuinely-open questions that should be revisited at each implementation slice. Note (closes 024A R2 R2-NEW-MAJ-001 / CMP-MAJ-004): earlier draft of this criterion said "(10 questions)"; fix-round-1 trimmed §10 from 10 entries to 3 (Q1 Renovate coverage / Q2 WP-SCP-025 successor / Q3 --restore test surface). Resolved-at-plan-doc-level entries do NOT belong in §10 — they're embodied in §2 invariants, §5 architecture, or §9 reservations. The DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance check is "§10 contains only genuinely-open questions; resolved questions are in their proper sections."' The stale '(10 questions)' count is gone; the acceptance check is reframed as a qualitative criterion consistent with the trimmed §10 (which contains 3 genuinely open questions at plan-doc line 239-243). The plan-doc §10 header note at line 239 corroborates: 'earlier drafts of this section listed 10 entries, 7 of which were resolved at plan-doc level... Below are the only genuinely open questions remaining at 024A merge.' DISPATCH-NOTE and plan-doc are now internally consistent on this point.

findings.title: R2-NEW-MAJ-002 closure: DISPATCH-NOTE line 36 stale '§10 Q7' and '§5.5' references replaced
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md scope-table row for '.github/workflows/scorecard-aggregator.yml extensions for cascade-status' (line 36) now reads: 'Aggregator extensions land at 024G if at all — may be rolled into existing consult_scorecard instead (D-046 to confirm; informational per §8, not part of Threshold A pass/fail). See §5.6 Threshold A telemetry.' Both stale references are gone: '§10 Q7' is absent (Q7 was removed when §10 was trimmed to 3 questions), and '§5.5' has been corrected to '§5.6' (the plan-doc's Threshold A telemetry section, which is the correct destination after the cross-repo coordination section was inserted as the new §5.5 by fix-round-1). The current plan-doc §5.6 (line 161) is indeed titled 'Threshold A telemetry' and covers the scorecard-aggregator / MCP-method decision. §8 at line 222 confirms the informational / non-Threshold-A-pass-fail framing: 'D-046 (at 024G) decides separately whether scp.consult_estate_status ships as a new MCP method or rolls into existing scp.consult_scorecard — that decision is informational at plan-doc time and is not part of the Threshold A pass/fail.' DISPATCH-NOTE line 36 and plan-doc are now internally consistent on this point.

findings.title: cascade-status field spec defines only two values but CI script enforcement requires distinguishing a third (operator-bump fallback) path with no parseable DISPATCH-NOTE signal
findings.evidence:
The plan-doc defines cascade-status: as a field taking exactly two values (§5.2 item (2), plan-doc line 111): 'onboarded' (success-path; enable-required-check.sh invoked) or 'blocked-on-adopter-conflict' (invariant-10 conflict-close; no invocation). The plan-doc then specifies a third check-path for the CI script in two places:

(1) §6 024B acceptance criteria (line 180): 'check-invocation-log-entry.sh parses DISPATCH-NOTE cascade-status: field and enforces both close-states — for onboarded: rejects PRs missing log entry / target mismatch; for blocked-on-adopter-conflict: requires TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> TF reference present in DISPATCH-NOTE; for the operator-bump fallback path (R-024-07): requires TF-024X-renovate-<adopter> STATUS.md row.'

(2) R-024-07 mitigation (line 199): 'the check-invocation-log-entry.sh CI script... verifies STATUS.md contains the matching TF row when DISPATCH-NOTE declares the operator-bump fallback.'

But §5.2 item (2) defines cascade-status: with only two values. There is no third value (e.g. 'onboarded-operator-bump') and no separate DISPATCH-NOTE field (e.g. 'version-propagation: operator-bump') defined anywhere in the plan-doc. The CI script cannot distinguish a cascade-status: onboarded slice that used a normal Renovate-driven bake from one that used an operator-driven SHA pin bump — both declare cascade-status: onboarded. The enforcement logic described in §6 024B ('for the operator-bump fallback path (R-024-07): requires TF-024X-renovate-<adopter> STATUS.md row') has no parseable trigger in the DISPATCH-NOTE protocol as specified.

This is an internal consistency defect introduced by the fix-round-2 edit that added the third check-path to §6 024B while leaving §5.2's two-value enum unchanged. The spec now describes CI enforcement behaviour that is unimplementable as written.
findings.recommendation: Extend the cascade-status: field spec in §5.2 item (2) to enumerate a third value: 'onboarded-operator-bump' (success-path via operator-driven SHA pin bump when Renovate is disabled; enable-required-check.sh invocation did occur; TF-024X-renovate-<adopter> STATUS.md row is filed). Update invariant 2 carve-out sentence and §6 024B acceptance criteria to name all three values explicitly. R-024-07 mitigation should be updated to state that cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump is what the CI script parses to apply the TF row verification. The three-value enum then maps cleanly to the three CI check-paths described in §6 024B.
